scope: Four bounded, individually sourced chronology strands. No cross-plane alignment, no absolute AR date conversion and no assertions that a narrated legend is historical fact. The New Phyrexia strand describes the early Mirrodin conquest as presented in Wizards' historical plane overview, not the post-March of the Machine political present.

neo_guide.title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty

strands.title: Kamigawa — the Kami War and early Imperial administration
strands.limitation: Only stated within the Neon Dynasty guide's historical summary. The Imperials' founding is not automatically chained to the boundary breakdown without a direct before/after statement.

strands.title: Bloomburrow Valley — narrated local legend, not established universal history
strands.limitation: The guide tells the Order of the Holly Leaf and Calamities history in an in-world voice and calls the Order legendary. Order here is the order of the tradition's account, not proved historical sequence or an AR calendar.

strands.title: Mirrodin to early New Phyrexia — corruption, conquest and Karn's restoration
strands.limitation: Only the official New Phyrexia plane overview's retrospective early-Mirrodin account. Its historical-present praetor politics are not a statement about present-day New Phyrexia after March of the Machine. This does not establish a complete war timeline, cross-plane synchrony or the precise order of Mirran defeat versus Venser's sacrifice.

strands.title: Duskmourn — the original House, Marina and the Ascension
strands.limitation: The guide's origin account does not specify an original plane name, AR date, post-2024 exit or present-day political status.

edges.source_title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty
edges.quote: Konda, Lord of Eiganjo, captured and imprisoned a part of O-Kagachi, the mightiest kami of Kamigawa. Enraged, O-Kagachi retaliated, plunging the mortal and spirit realms into a decades-long war.
edges.note: Retaliation follows the imprisonment; no absolute year.

edges.source_title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty
edges.quote: The imprisoned part of O-Kagachi broke free and became a new kami named Kyodai.
edges.note: The fragment had to be imprisoned before it escaped.

edges.source_title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty
edges.quote: The imprisoned part of O-Kagachi broke free and became a new kami named Kyodai. Kyodai partnered with Konda's daughter, Michiko, to defeat both O-Kagachi and Konda.
edges.note: The account presents Kyodai's emergence before the victory.

edges.source_title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty
edges.quote: Kyodai partnered with Konda's daughter, Michiko, to defeat both O-Kagachi and Konda. The death of O-Kagachi caused the barrier between the two realms to break down
edges.note: The boundary rupture follows O-Kagachi's death in the narrated victory; does not order the individual defeats.

edges.source_title: Planeswalker's Guide to Kamigawa: Neon Dynasty
edges.quote: founded to help Kyodai manage the merging of the mortal and spirit realms. Over time, they expanded into government and rulership.
edges.note: Explicit 'Over time' after the institution's initial mission.

edges.quote: The oppressive heel of the Calamities imposed an unstable equality, a reason for those who could not contend with their power alone to band together.
edges.note: The storyteller describes animalfolk banding together in response to the Calamities.

edges.quote: Discontented to live their lives in the deep tunnels beneath Valley, a band was formed
edges.note: The narrated underground life precedes the formation of the Order.

edges.quote: However, their pact had another consequence. The land was now a wellspring of energy for them to draw from.
edges.note: The narrator says the magical transformation followed the pact.

edges.quote: Powerful as weaving was, the Calamity Beasts would not succumb to their terrible new powers. For two generations, battles raged throughout Valley.
edges.note: The account says weaving existed when two generations of battles began.

edges.quote: It was then that the greatest among the Calamities appeared: Wildsear
edges.note: The storyteller situates Wildsear's appearance during the war; 'then' does not prove the whole war ended first.

edges.quote: The animalfolk grew indulgent in the seasons after Lily has saved them. Weaving grew too powerful
edges.note: The excess weaving is explicitly after Lily's rescue in the traditional account.

edges.quote: In response to the chaos that weaving had wrought, the lineage of heroes chose to seal their most powerful knowledge away.
edges.note: The sealing follows and responds to the dangerous backlashes.

edges.quote: which began the slow process of transforming the creatures it touched deep beneath the world's surface
edges.note: The overview directly links the brought oil to the ensuing transformation; no exact transmission date is supplied.

edges.quote: The slow spread soon became an active campaign to alter, or compleat, the world of Mirrodin.
edges.note: The gradual oil spread precedes the described active campaign; this does not order every individual infection.

edges.quote: The Mirrans fought many battles, but they soon were overwhelmed by the Phyrexian forces.
edges.note: The Mirrans' response is to the active Phyrexian campaign named immediately before this sentence; not a start date for every Mirran battle.

edges.quote: The Mirrans fought many battles, but they soon were overwhelmed by the Phyrexian forces.
edges.note: The overview distinguishes sustained resistance from its early defeat; this does not mean all Mirrans died or resistance permanently ended.

edges.quote: Even the Planeswalkers Koth, Elspeth, and Venser could not turn the tide, and Venser sacrificed his life to restore Karn to sanity.
edges.note: Planeswalker efforts to turn the tide precede the described sacrifice; no claim is made that all Mirran resistance ended before it.

edges.quote: Venser sacrificed his life to restore Karn to sanity
edges.note: Karn's prior corrupted leadership is the state restored from; the overview does not synchronize his ascent with each phase of Mirrodin's conquest.

edges.quote: Trapped and unable to feed, the demon had sunk into hibernation and bided his time—until Marina came along and unwittingly loosened his shackles.
edges.note: The binding and hibernation precede Marina's involvement.

edges.quote: However, it was already too late. People around Marina began to meet sudden, unexplained, and terrifying ends. The neighborhood began to warp as well
edges.note: The neighborhood's distortion follows the basement victims in the guide's account.

edges.quote: But then, her parents vanished. Unable to deny it any longer, she delved into research
edges.note: Marina investigates once the spreading horrors and disappearances become undeniable.

edges.quote: Faced with the full truth at last of what she had done, Marina confronted the entity and demanded it stop.
edges.note: Her discovery precedes the confrontation.

edges.quote: With no other choice, the demon agreed to give her back the world as she remembered it.
edges.note: The false restoration follows Marina's ultimatum.

edges.quote: In reality, the house continued to expand. The horrors continued to increase, drowning all who lived within in terror. And the demon grew in power, until the entirety of the plane was swallowed up in the walls of Duskmourn.
edges.note: While Marina saw a false restoration, the House expanded into the Ascension.

known_gaps: No primary-source edge joins distinct strand IDs, so cross-plane comparisons remain UNKNOWN.
Valley events order an explicitly legendary in-world account, not objectively certified ancient history.

New Phyrexia events describe early Mirrodin conquest; the source does not order the complete war, the Mirrans being overwhelmed against Venser's sacrifice, or the political present after March of the Machine.
A DURING_OR_AFTER_START relation is not a strict BEFORE edge and never participates in transitive ordering.
Unknown original plane names, absolute AR years and missing historical events are not supplied.
This source-local supplement does not replace the original Packs A–C chronology or certify L244.
